title: Article: Mantra vs Meditation: Two Paths to Spiritual Energy | Ashaeiynn

segments.text: Two paths to the same destination—but do they work in the same way?
One of the most common questions among spiritual seekers is:
Can mantra chanting give the same power and energy as meditation?
And if both are powerful spiritual practices, can they be practiced together?
At first glance, both seem very similar. Both help a person grow spiritually. Both generate spiritual energy. Both can eventually lead a seeker toward higher states of consciousness.
Yet, according to Guru Tattva, they are not the same.
Some spiritual traditions primarily follow mantra chanting.
Others place greater emphasis on meditation.
There are also traditions where both are practiced together—but only under specific conditions.
So before asking which path is better, we must first understand how each path actually works.
Before Choosing a Path
Not every spiritual practice is meant for everyone.
People often ask,
“Should I meditate or should I chant mantras?”
According to Guru Tattva, the answer depends entirely on the individual.
Both paths generate spiritual energy, but they do so in completely different ways.
Unless we understand that difference, choosing the right path becomes difficult.
So let us begin by understanding the hidden science of meditation.
The Hidden Science of Meditation
What really happens when a person meditates?
Most people think meditation simply means sitting quietly with closed eyes.
According to Guru Tattva, meditation is much more than that.
Meditation is a process in which a person gradually combines their own consciousness with the Universal Cosmos Energy continuously flowing through the universe.
But this process cannot happen on its own.
It depends upon two essential elements:
Aura – the subtle energy field surrounding the body.
Vital Essence (Veerya) – the inner force preserved through disciplined living.
Without these two, meditation cannot produce its full effect.
The stronger these two become, the greater the power of meditation.
How Does Meditation Create Spiritual Gravity?
The invisible force that connects dimensions.
When a person enters meditation, something subtle begins to happen.
The Universal Cosmos Energy naturally falling upon the practitioner begins to unite with the person’s Vital Essence.
When these two merge, they create a powerful gravitational pull.
According to Guru Tattva, this is the real power of meditation.
This gravity is what allows a person’s consciousness to connect with higher dimensions.
The stronger the gravity, the farther that connection can reach.
Understanding Meditation Through a Simple Example
Why can some voices reach farther than others?
Imagine two people standing on different buildings.
The first person stands on the fifth floor and shouts loudly.
His voice reaches people standing several floors above him.
Now imagine another person shouting with much less strength.
His voice cannot even reach the floor directly above him.
Both tried to call someone.
But only one person’s voice travelled farther.
Why?
Because one had greater strength.
Meditation works in a similar way.
The “voice” in meditation is not sound—it is your spiritual gravity.
The stronger your gravity becomes, the higher the dimensions your consciousness can reach.
Someone with weaker gravity may only connect to lower levels.
Someone with stronger gravity can connect much farther.
The Power of Invocation
How prayers reach higher realms.
According to Guru Tattva, this gravitational pull is also known as the Power of Invocation.
Every time a person prays or directs their Kundalini Shakti upward, that prayer can travel only as far as their spiritual gravity allows.
Think of it like throwing a ball into the sky.
A child may throw it only a few feet.
A trained athlete can throw it much higher.
The destination depends on the strength behind the throw.
Similarly, prayers, meditation, and Kundalini Shakti can only reach the dimensions that a person’s gravitational pull is capable of touching.
The greater the gravity, the higher the connection.
The Fuel Behind Meditation
Why do great meditators give so much importance to celibacy?
After understanding how meditation creates spiritual gravity, another important question arises:
What determines the strength of that gravity?
According to Guru Tattva, two things work together to create the power of meditation:
Universal Cosmos Energy constantly flowing toward the practitioner.
Vital Essence (Veerya) preserved within the body.
Meditation becomes powerful only when these two combine.When they unite, they generate the gravitational pull that allows a person’s consciousness to connect with higher dimensions.
Why Is Celibacy So Important?
Protecting the fuel that powers spiritual gravity
Think of meditation like flying a hot-air balloon.
The balloon may be perfectly built, but without enough fuel, it can never rise into the sky.
According to Guru Tattva, Vital Essence is that fuel.
The more a person preserves it through disciplined living and celibacy, the stronger the gravitational pull created during meditation.
If the Vital Essence becomes weak or is constantly depleted, the gravitational force also weakens.
As a result, the person’s ability to connect with higher dimensions gradually decreases.
This is why celibacy has always been considered one of the most important disciplines for practitioners following the path of meditation.
The Role of Universal Cosmos Energy
The energy that every human continuously receives
According to Guru Tattva, every person constantly receives Universal Cosmos Energy.
The amount and timing of this energy are influenced by the planetary energies active in that person’s life.
Anyone born through the natural cycle of birth remains connected to these planetary influences.
Meditation works by combining this incoming Universal Cosmos Energy with the person’s preserved Vital Essence.
From this union, spiritual gravity is created.
And from that gravity, higher spiritual connection becomes possible.
Why Saints Chose a Life of Discipline
The secret hidden behind ancient Tapasya
Ancient scriptures often describe great saints leaving their homes and living in forests or mountains.
Why did they choose such a difficult life?
According to Guru Tattva, their goal was to preserve their Vital Essence and devote themselves completely to meditation.
The Universal Cosmos Energy they received was continuously combined with their preserved Vital Essence, creating an increasingly powerful gravitational pull.
According to this understanding, their spiritual gravity became so strong that it could even draw the attention of higher divine realms.
This is why many ancient scriptures describe the throne of Indra beginning to tremble whenever a great sage performed intense Tapasya.
The Mystery of the Celestial Maidens
Why were sages tested?
Ancient scriptures often describe Celestial Maidens (Apsaras) being sent to interrupt the meditation of great sages.
According to Guru Tattva, their purpose was not simply to distract the sages.
It was to break their celibacy.
The moment the Vital Essence was lost, the source that powered their meditation weakened.
Without that inner fuel, the powerful gravitational pull they had been building could no longer continue in the same way.
This is why preserving celibacy became such an important discipline for meditation.
But What About Ordinary People?
Is meditation possible for everyone?
Now another important question naturally arises.
Not everyone can maintain celibacy throughout life.
Many people live as householders.
Others may find it difficult to preserve their Vital Essence consistently.
Does that mean spiritual progress becomes impossible?
According to Guru Tattva—
No.
The ancient saints found another path.
A path that did not depend entirely on preserving Vital Essence.
That discovery became the foundation of Mantra Shakti.
The Discovery of Mantra Shakti
A new way to preserve spiritual energy
The saints understood that although many people could not preserve their Vital Essence permanently, they still generated spiritual energy every day.
Instead of allowing that energy to be lost, they found a way to preserve it.
According to Guru Tattva, that preservation happens through mantra chanting.
Every sincere repetition gradually stores the practitioner’s spiritual energy within the mantra itself.
Instead of depending on the Vital Essence every time, the mantra slowly begins to hold that accumulated energy.
How Does a Mantra Become Powerful?
Small efforts become great strength over time
Imagine filling a water tank with just one bucket of water every day.
One bucket seems insignificant.
But after many years, the tank becomes completely full.
Mantra chanting works in a similar way.
Each repetition adds a little more spiritual strength to the mantra.
Day after day…
Month after month…
Year after year…
The accumulated energy continues growing.
This stored spiritual strength is known as Mantra Shakti.
When the Mantra Becomes the Source
The difference between meditation and mantra chanting
Here lies the greatest difference between the two paths.
In meditation, the gravitational pull is created through the union of Universal Cosmos Energy and Vital Essence.
In mantra chanting, the gradually accumulated Mantra Shakti itself becomes the source of that gravitational pull.
Because the mantra now carries the stored energy, the practitioner no longer depends on invoking the Vital Essence each time.
Instead, they invoke the power already preserved within the mantra.
This is why, according to Guru Tattva, celibacy is not considered essential for the path of mantra chanting in the same way it is for meditation.
The Hidden Secret Behind Guru Parampara
What exactly is passed from a Guru to a disciple?
Until now, we have understood that continuous mantra chanting gradually stores spiritual energy within the mantra itself.
But another fascinating question arises.
If a person spends an entire lifetime strengthening one mantra, what happens to all that accumulated Mantra Shakti after them?
According to Guru Tattva, that energy is not lost.
It becomes the foundation of Guru Parampara.
How Is Mantra Shakti Passed On?
A spiritual inheritance beyond words
Imagine someone planting a tree and caring for it every day for fifty years.
When the next generation arrives, they do not receive a tiny seed.
They receive a fully grown tree.
According to Guru Tattva, Guru Parampara works in a similar way.
If a practitioner spends their entire life chanting one mantra, the spiritual energy accumulated through that chanting becomes associated with the mantra itself.
When that mantra is initiated into a disciple or passed on to future generations, it is not merely the words that are being transferred.
The disciple also receives the Mantra Shakti that has been preserved through years of sincere practice.
In this way, the Guru passes on the spiritual strength of an entire lifetime.
Why Different Guru Paramparas Exist
Every lineage carries its own spiritual current
This understanding explains why different Guru Paramparās were formed.
Some saints established the Gayatri Parampara.
Others established the Nath Parampara.
Each lineage continuously strengthened a particular mantra generation after generation.
Every Guru added their own spiritual energy to that mantra before passing it to the next disciple.
As a result, the Mantra Shakti of the lineage continued becoming stronger with time.
The more spiritual energy preserved within a mantra, the greater its gravitational pull.
Meditation and Guru Parampara
Why the two paths preserve different things
This is another important difference between meditation and mantra chanting.
According to Guru Tattva, meditation does not transfer accumulated spiritual gravity from one person to another.
Instead, a meditation master helps expand the disciple’s consciousness and guides them toward higher dimensions through personal practice.
Mantra chanting works differently.
Here, the mantra itself carries the accumulated Mantra Shakti of the lineage.
The disciple receives not only guidance but also a spiritual current that has already been strengthened over generations.
The Power Hidden Within a Mantra
Why invocation becomes so powerful
A person who follows the path of mantra chanting continuously nourishes the same mantra throughout life.
Over time, the mantra becomes filled with accumulated spiritual gravity.
According to Guru Tattva, whenever that practitioner invokes the mantra, they also invoke the entire Mantra Shakti stored within it.
The gravitational pull created at that moment is not limited to today’s chanting alone.
It also draws upon the spiritual energy accumulated through years of continuous practice.
This is why continuous mantra chanting is given so much importance.
Meditation or Mantra—Which Is Greater?
Two paths, two methods, one destination
Naturally, another question arises.
Which path is superior?
According to Guru Tattva, neither.
Both ultimately lead the practitioner toward Samadhi, the state where one begins experiencing Param Tattva completely.
The difference lies only in the method.
Meditation develops spiritual gravity through the union of Universal Cosmos Energy and Vital Essence.
Mantra chanting develops spiritual gravity through the continuous strengthening of Mantra Shakti.
One depends upon preserving Vital Essence.
The other depends upon preserving the mantra.
The destination is the same.
The journey is different.
The Stages of Spiritual Growth
Every path unfolds step by step
According to Guru Tattva, spiritual growth never happens instantly.
The path of mantra chanting unfolds through six stages, eventually leading the practitioner toward Samadhi.
Similarly, meditation also progresses through different stages, and Samadhi itself is described in multiple forms.
No matter which path a seeker chooses, growth happens gradually.
Can Both Paths Be Practiced Together?
A question that confuses many seekers
After understanding both systems, many people ask:
“Why not practice meditation and mantra chanting together?”
Some practitioners do exactly that.
But according to Guru Tattva, combining both paths without proper understanding can create serious problems.
The reason is simple.
Both practices generate spiritual gravity through different mechanisms.
Meditation depends upon Vital Essence.
Mantra chanting gradually depends upon Mantra Shakti.
If these systems are mixed incorrectly, energetic imbalance may occur.
When Does Mantra Chanting Become Meditation?
The difference of chanting between the mouth and the mind
Guru Tattva explains an important distinction that many practitioners overlook.
When a mantra is chanted aloud, the vibrations are produced mainly through the mouth.
But when the chanting becomes completely mental, the process changes.
At that stage, every part of the body begins participating in generating the vibration.
According to Guru Tattva, a person with an awakened Third Eye can observe these vibrations spreading throughout the practitioner’s entire body.
Mental chanting therefore creates a much stronger energetic field than verbal chanting.
But with greater energy comes greater responsibility.
The Hidden Danger of Mental Chanting
Why protection becomes essential
As soon as mantra chanting becomes completely mental, it begins functioning much like meditation.
And meditation follows one important rule.
Vital Essence must be preserved.
According to Guru Tattva, Vital Essence does more than generate spiritual gravity.
It also protects the practitioner’s aura.
If a person practices mental chanting without maintaining this protection, the aura gradually becomes vulnerable.
Why Negative Entities Become Attracted
The vibration they are searching for
A natural question arises.
Why would mental chanting attract negative entities?
According to Guru Tattva, the attraction is created by the vibration itself.
Every mental repetition produces subtle vibrations that spread far beyond the physical body.
These vibrations are believed to be perceptible to astral beings.
Most may simply observe.
But negative entities are described as constantly searching for powerful sources of spiritual energy.
If the practitioner’s aura is no longer protected by preserved Vital Essence, those vibrations become an open invitation.
How Spiritual Energy Can Be Lost
When someone else begins using your effort
According to Guru Tattva, once a negative entity becomes attached to the practitioner, it begins drawing upon the energy produced through meditation.
The practitioner may believe they are progressing toward the Divine.
But in reality, much of the spiritual energy they generate is being consumed elsewhere.
Over time, such an entity may even misguide the seeker by appearing helpful or pretending to be a divine presence.
For this reason, Guru Tattva repeatedly advises that meditation and mental mantra chanting should never be mixed carelessly.
When Can Both Be Practiced Together?
Only under the guidance of Guru Tattva
Does this mean mantra chanting and meditation should never be combined?
According to Guru Tattva—
They can.
But only under proper guidance.
The practitioner must understand both systems, preserve Vital Essence, and follow the discipline required for meditation.
Only then can both paths work together safely.
A Final Mystery of Meditation
Which negativity can take the energy generated through meditation?
According to Guru Tattva, when a saint enters Samadhi, their spiritual gravity becomes so powerful that no new negative entity can approach them.

During Samadhi, the practitioner maintains complete celibacy, allowing the Vital Essence to remain preserved. As long as the Vital Essence is intact, the spiritual energy generated through meditation remains protected, and no entity can draw upon it.
However, there is one important exception.

If a negative entity had already become attached to the practitioner before entering Samadhi, it remains connected throughout the entire period of meditation. It cannot interfere with the Samadhi itself, but it continues to remain attached.

After the Samadhi is complete, if the practitioner breaks celibacy and loses the Vital Essence, the protection created by that Vital Essence is removed. At that moment, the same negative entity that was attached before the Samadhi can draw upon the entire spiritual energy accumulated during that period of meditation.

This is why Guru Tattva places so much importance on maintaining celibacy for those who follow the path of meditation. It is not only necessary for generating spiritual gravity but also for preserving the spiritual energy earned through meditation. Otherwise, the energy accumulated over months or even years can be taken away.

According to Guru Tattva, no new negative entity can take that energy. Only the negativity that was already attached to the practitioner before the meditation or Samadhi began can draw upon the spiritual energy accumulated through it.
The Final Understanding
Choose the path wisely, not quickly.
Both mantra chanting and meditation are complete spiritual paths.
Both can eventually lead to Samadhi.
Both can help a seeker realize Param Tattva.
The difference is not the destination.
The difference lies in how spiritual gravity is created, preserved, and protected.
Understanding that difference is what allows a seeker to choose the path best suited to their own spiritual journey.
